chunks: Ali, from his father, by his chain, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever swears secretly, let him make his exception secretly, and whoever swears publicly, let him make his exception publicly.'
ai.seo_question: How should one make an exception in an oath according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural etiquette of *istithna'* (exception) in oaths, emphasizing that the visibility of the exception must match the visibility of the oath to ensure legal validity and clarity. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction prevents ambiguity in whether the oath was effectively broken or modified, reflecting the Prophet’s attention to social context in legal rulings. It underscores the principle that religious obligations often adapt to the public or private nature of the act to maintain integrity and avoid confusion.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, by his chain from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who swears secretly, so let him (say the) exclusion secretly, and the one who swear publicly, so let him (say the) exclusion publicly’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali has narrated from his father from through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the following is narrated from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If one takes an oath privately, he must make the exception privately; and if one takes an oath in public, he must make the exception in public.’”
